name: Revyl

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

caveats: Free 1 concurrent device per platform; Starter $250/mo includes $250 credits/3 devices, Team Pro $750 with $750/10; annual $200/$600. Overage enabled: iOS $0.15/min, Android $0.12/min. LLM uses same allowance. Enterprise dedicated iOS runners; no 4/8 sizing guaranteed.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Overage is billed only 'when enabled' (likely a toggle; default state not stated): without it, usage stops at the plan allowance. LLM (agent) usage draws down the same compute-credit allowance. Remote cloud builds also consume metered compute credits at unpublished rates.
Team Pro adds a priority device queue; Free/Starter share the standard queue (queueing, not billing). Dedicated iOS runners/instances are Enterprise/sales only.

fleet.tiers: Free 1 concurrent device per platform, Starter 3, Team Pro 10, Enterprise unlimited.
fleet.notes: Pricing variants conflict: ?plan=free describes 1 device per platform and Starter 3, while canonical page now calls entry tier Solo. Using conservative canonical one-device baseline; confirm actual subscription before large fleet.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Sessions auto-terminate after 5 minutes of idle time. Call `start_device_session` to provision a new device.
snapshot_auto.note: Device sessions (iOS simulators / Android emulators) end on idle timeout or stop and the next session is a newly provisioned device; no state save/restore for users. Revyl uses snapshot-restore internally for isolation ('Simulators (iOS) and emulators (Android) give us isolation and snapshot-restore'), which is not a user feature.

own_agent_api.quote: Launch app exploration, follow each explorer, and produce an Atlas map from a terminal or CI job.
own_agent_api.note: Borderline: harness = Revyl's own device-operating AI agent, not a coding agent inside a sandbox. CLI/API/MCP start it with natural-language input (`revyl explore run --instructions ...`, `revyl device instruction "Open Settings and tap Wi-Fi"`, `revyl device validation ...`), show progress, status/cancel; Proof of Changes runs the Revyl agent per PR (`harness.kind: revyl` or `cursor`). Revyl can also launch Cursor Cloud Agent conversations and track them under Cloud Agents, but 'The agent runs in Cursor's cloud'. No Claude Code/Codex harness hosted by Revyl.

harness_api.quote: Launch app exploration, follow each explorer, and produce an Atlas map from a terminal or CI job.
harness_api.note: Borderline: harness = Revyl's own device-operating AI agent, not a coding agent inside a sandbox. CLI/API/MCP start it with natural-language input (`revyl explore run --instructions ...`, `revyl device instruction "Open Settings and tap Wi-Fi"`, `revyl device validation ...`), show progress, status/cancel; Proof of Changes runs the Revyl agent per PR (`harness.kind: revyl` or `cursor`). Revyl can also launch Cursor Cloud Agent conversations and track them under Cloud Agents, but 'The agent runs in Cursor's cloud'. No Claude Code/Codex harness hosted by Revyl.

guest_firewall.quote: the platform only permits that against debuggable apps on non-rooted (Play-image) emulators
guest_firewall.note: Users get iOS simulators and non-rooted Android emulators on shared hosts, no root/shell on the host. Exception: Enterprise 'Revyl computer' dedicated Macs (revyl-computer ssh) give 'passwordless `sudo`' on an org-shared machine whose disk persists, where pf would presumably work (not documented).

secret_proxy.quote: Secret payloads can only be replaced, not viewed.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are encrypted write-only launch variables / global variables / build secret references, delivered into the app launch environment, test steps or build env. No injecting proxy.

isolation.quote: Cloud test infra runs on shared hosts. Simulators (iOS) and emulators (Android) give us isolation and snapshot-restore.
isolation.note: Revyl runs iOS Simulator / Android Emulator processes on shared hosts (no per-customer hypervisor VM is described); process/app-sandbox isolation is the closest fit to the given taxonomy. A separate Enterprise 'Revyl Computer' product gives shell access to dedicated, org-shared Mac hardware, which is a different isolation model not covered by this single field.

image_oci.quote: Revyl runs tests on cloud simulators (iOS) and emulators (Android), not physical devices.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Machines are started from uploaded mobile app builds (.apk/.app), not customer-supplied Docker/OCI images.

docker_inside.quote: Revyl provides cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators that you can provision, control, and observe from your own tools.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Device sessions are mobile OS simulators/emulators; no documented ability to run arbitrary containers inside them.

nested_virt.quote: Revyl provides cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators that you can provision, control, and observe from your own tools.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No user-facing /dev/kvm or nested-VM capability is documented for device sessions.

desktop.quote: Revyl gives you cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators, an optional AI agent that tests your app using natural language, and tooling to run it all in CI.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The streamed surface is a mobile device screen (iOS/Android), not a general graphical desktop; the Enterprise 'Revyl Computer' Mac is shell-only (no GUI/VNC/RDP).

browser.quote: Revyl gives you cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators, an optional AI agent that tests your app using natural language, and tooling to run it all in CI.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Product is mobile app device testing; no managed browser is provided (device_navigate can open a URL/deep link on the mobile OS's own browser app, but Revyl does not manage/provide a browser).

anti_bot.quote: Revyl drives your app from cloud devices, so traffic to your backend comes from Revyl's infrastructure rather than a typical user's network. ... that traffic can get blocked.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope, and the opposite of stealth -- Revyl asks customers to allowlist its known static IPs so its own testing traffic is NOT flagged as a bot.

captcha_solving.quote: Allowlist Revyl's IP addresses in your rate limiter, WAF, or CAPTCHA provider to prevent this.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Revyl's documented approach to CAPTCHA is asking the customer to allowlist Revyl's IPs, not solving CAPTCHAs itself.

egress_ip_type.quote: Traffic from Revyl's backend comes from the following static IP addresses today: iOS devices: 50.112.63.125 Android devices: 136.117.185.7

ssh.quote: revyl-computer ssh ... Revyl brokers the connection, so no SSH client, AWS Session Manager plugin, SSH key, or cloud credentials are required.
ssh.note: Brokered shell access (not raw SSH protocol) to Enterprise 'Revyl Computer' dedicated Mac hardware, with passwordless sudo. Regular iOS/Android device sessions have no shell/SSH access.

snapshot.quote: Sessions auto-terminate after 5 minutes of idle time. Call `start_device_session` to provision a new device.
snapshot.note: No user-facing snapshot/checkpoint API for device sessions; the next session is a freshly provisioned device, not a restored one. Revyl uses simulator/emulator snapshot-restore internally for its own isolation, not as a customer feature.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Sessions auto-terminate after 5 minutes of idle time. Call `start_device_session` to provision a new device.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No documented API/CLI command to take an on-demand snapshot/checkpoint of a device session.

pause_resume.note: Device session lifecycle is start/stop only; no pause/resume tool or command documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Sessions auto-terminate after 5 minutes of idle time. Call `start_device_session` to provision a new device.
wake_on_request.note: An idled/stopped session must be explicitly re-provisioned by calling start_device_session again; nothing wakes it automatically on an inbound request.

persistent_disk.quote: The machine is shared by your whole organization and its disk persists between sessions, so anything you install or change stays there for your teammates and for later runs.
persistent_disk.note: True for the Enterprise 'Revyl Computer' dedicated Mac (org-shared, persistent disk). Regular iOS/Android device sessions are ephemeral/freshly provisioned with no documented persistent disk.

volume_attach.quote: Revyl gives you cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators, an optional AI agent that tests your app using natural language, and tooling to run it all in CI.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No attachable extra-volume feature is documented.

volume_shared.quote: Revyl gives you cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators, an optional AI agent that tests your app using natural language, and tooling to run it all in CI.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Sessions auto-terminate after 5 minutes of idle time.
auto_stop_idle.note: Also true for Revyl Computer shells: "A shell with no activity closes after 60 minutes, and every shell closes after 24 hours."

live_resize.quote: Revyl gives you cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators, an optional AI agent that tests your app using natural language, and tooling to run it all in CI.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Mobile simulator/emulator device sessions have no documented CPU/RAM resize while running.

agent_harnesses.quote: Connect Revyl over MCP so your coding agent can run the current app source, control cloud devices, and verify changes.
agent_harnesses.note: Revyl integrates with external coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) that call into Revyl via MCP/CLI plugins; it does not preinstall or host a coding-agent harness inside its own sandboxes.

mcp_server.quote: Connect Revyl to Cursor, Claude Code, or Codex ... The Revyl MCP server exposes tools across the following categories.

lang_python.quote: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Bash are all supported.
lang_python.note: Also has a first-party Python SDK (`pip install revyl[sdk]`) per the CLI quickstart.

lang_node.quote: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Bash are all supported.
lang_node.note: Node.js is also present in remote-build toolchain images (e.g. Node.js 22.23.0).

public_ipv4.quote: The host running your CLI or agent does not need a local simulator ... Use remote builds to compile your app in the cloud too.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Devices are reached only through Revyl's authenticated API/CLI/MCP and viewer link, not a public IPv4 address.

inbound_https.quote: Your code decides what happens on it. ... Existing Android emulator / iOS simulator session
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No user-controlled HTTPS ingress to ports on the device; the embeddable live device is Revyl's own viewer iframe, not general port exposure.

ingress_rules.quote: Your code decides what happens on it. ... Existing Android emulator / iOS simulator session
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No exposed ports to control access to.

egress_allowlist.quote: Allowlist Revyl's IP addresses in your rate limiter, WAF, or CAPTCHA provider to prevent this.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side control found for restricting a device session's own outbound traffic; the documented allowlisting is the customer's own backend allowlisting Revyl's fixed outbound IPs, not the reverse.

egress_http_rules.quote: Allowlist Revyl's IP addresses in your rate limiter, WAF, or CAPTCHA provider to prevent this.
egress_http_rules.note: No method/path-level egress rule feature found.

static_egress_ip.quote: Traffic from Revyl's backend comes from the following static IP addresses today: iOS devices: 50.112.63.125 Android devices: 136.117.185.7

gpu.quote: Revyl gives you cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators, an optional AI agent that tests your app using natural language, and tooling to run it all in CI.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No GPU compute machines are offered; this is a mobile simulator/emulator testing platform.

windows.quote: Revyl runs tests on cloud simulators (iOS) and emulators (Android), not physical devices.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No Windows machines/devices are offered (Windows is only supported as a client OS for installing the CLI/revyl-computer binary).

arm64.quote: Ubuntu | 24.04 (arm64, with Rosetta translation for x86_64 binaries)
arm64.note: Android remote-build runners are arm64; iOS build/simulator infra runs on Apple Silicon (arm64) Macs.

self_host.quote: Revyl gives you cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators, an optional AI agent that tests your app using natural language, and tooling to run it all in CI.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Revyl is a hosted SaaS; no self-hosting option is documented.

byoc.quote: Revyl gives you cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators, an optional AI agent that tests your app using natural language, and tooling to run it all in CI.

open_source.note: Core platform is closed-source SaaS. The public revyl-cli repo carries no OSI license, so even the CLI is not formally open source.

max_session_h.quote: Sessions also close on their own after an hour of inactivity, and after 24 hours in any case.
max_session_h.note: This is the clearest documented hard session cap, for Enterprise 'Revyl Computer' Mac shells. Regular iOS/Android device sessions default to a 5-minute idle timeout (configurable) with no documented absolute hard cap found; the live-device embed caps active time at 10 minutes.
